feedback: If a learner tags every human-caused card as 'bad' and natural cards as 'fine', remind them a fast natural flood or fire is also dangerous, and some human changes are slow.

If a learner picks a rooted plant or slow specialist as the fast-change survivor, revisit 'could it move away in time?' and ask whether it already tolerates the new conditions — if not, it is unlikely to survive.
activities.intendedInsight: Changes come in kinds (natural/human-caused) and speeds (slow/fast). The organisms most likely to survive a FAST change are mobile ones that can escape in time to suitable habitat within reach, or ones that already tolerate the new conditions. Rooted plants and slow or specialised organisms cannot escape a fast change, and may still struggle when change is slow. Slow change gives more time to move to suitable habitat and is the only kind that allows a population to shift over many generations; fast change leaves no time for that generational shift and little time to escape.
learnerActions: Sort change cards (seasonal drought, flood, fire, hard winter, disease, pond drained, woodland cleared, pollution, a new road) into NATURAL vs HUMAN-CAUSED.
Sort the same cards a second way along a SLOW vs FAST axis.
Put a set of cards in order to build one cause → effect → knock-on chain for a familiar organism (frog, heron, hedgehog, oak).
Answer and justify: 'Which organism is most likely to survive a fast change, and why?'
activities.title: Sort the changes, order the chain

feedback: If the learner only narrates 'the pond dried', prompt for the next link: 'and so what happened to the heron?'
activities.intendedInsight: Putting the reasoning into words — naming the change, the affected organism, and the knock-on effect — makes the causal chain repeatable and checks your own understanding.
learnerActions: After exploring a change, ask a ranger or naturalist character questions like 'What happened to the frogs when the pond dried?' and 'Why couldn't the reeds move away?'
Explain back, in your own words, one knock-on chain you discovered.
activities.title: Ask the pond ranger (optional debrief)
